idiom_name: primary constructor with named and default arguments (+ @DslMarker lambda builders for nested trees)
implementation_notes: Kotlin's primary constructor with named arguments and default values already provides what a Java staged builder provides - unskippable required parameters and named optional ones - in a single call, so the staged chain is normally unnecessary and a data class plus copy() covers variations of a built value. When a builder is still warranted (nested hierarchies, side-effecting setup, or an API shared with Java callers), the Kotlin form is a lambda-with-receiver DSL whose receiver types model the stages, with @DslMarker stopping outer-scope members from leaking into inner blocks. Keep the classic step interface chain only when the API is consumed from a language that cannot use named arguments.
pitfalls: Named arguments stop misplacement but not wrong values: type and presence checking is not validation, so add require()/init-block checks for domain rules.
A lambda DSL with nested receivers needs @DslMarker; without it inner blocks can call outer-step functions and the staging guarantee leaks.
scope functions are not stages: apply/also return the same receiver, so the compiler cannot see the order and required setup degrades to runtime checks.
